verbs.ex: We hope to close the deal before the end of the quarter.
They finally struck a deal after three rounds of talks.
A quick call with the CFO sealed the deal.

note.de: „Einen Deal abschließen“ heißt close a deal, nicht finish.
note.en: "Close" is the verb for completing a deal, not "finish".

verbs.ex: We met the deadline with two days to spare.
If we miss the deadline, we lose the discount.
Could you extend the deadline to Friday?

note.de: „Eine Frist einhalten“ heißt meet a deadline.
note.en: You meet a deadline; you do not "keep" it.

verbs.ex: We need to make a decision by Monday.
The board reached a decision after a long discussion.
They postponed the decision until next quarter.

note.de: „Eine Entscheidung treffen“ heißt make a decision.
note.en: You make a decision; "meet" is a literal translation of "treffen".

verbs.ex: We hold a team meeting every Monday.
Who is going to run the meeting today?
Let's schedule a meeting for next week.
The CFO will attend the meeting in person.

note.de: Meetings hat, hält oder leitet man: have, hold, run.
note.en: You have, hold, or run a meeting; you do not "make" one.

verbs.ex: I am giving a presentation to the board tomorrow.
She delivered a clear presentation in ten minutes.
I need the numbers to prepare the presentation.

note.de: „Eine Präsentation halten“ heißt give a presentation.
note.en: You give or deliver a presentation; "hold" is a German pattern.

verbs.ex: Can I ask a question about the price?
The audit raised a few questions about our archive.
I will answer your question after the demo.

note.de: „Eine Frage stellen“ heißt ask a question.
note.en: You ask a question; you do not "make" one.

verbs.ex: Everyone makes mistakes in a new system.
We corrected the mistake in the invoice right away.
It takes courage to admit a mistake to a customer.

note.de: Fehler macht man mit make, nicht do.
note.en: Mistakes take "make", not "do".

verbs.ex: We can give you a discount for a three-year contract.
They offered a ten percent discount.
Procurement negotiated a small discount.

note.de: „Einen Rabatt machen“ heißt give oder offer a discount.
note.en: You give or offer a discount; "make" is a German pattern.

verbs.ex: We cannot lower the price without changing the scope.
Many vendors raised their prices this year.
Let's negotiate the price after the pilot.

note.de: „Den Preis senken“ heißt lower oder reduce the price.
note.en: You lower or reduce a price; "sink" does not work here.

verbs.ex: They signed the contract on Friday.
Most customers renew their contract after the first year.
You can terminate the contract with three months’ notice.

note.de: „Einen Vertrag kündigen“ heißt terminate oder cancel; quit sagt man beim Job.
note.en: To end a contract, use terminate or cancel; you quit a job.

verbs.ex: Could you take a photo of our booth?
I shared a photo of the team on LinkedIn.
We posted a photo from the trade show.

note.de: Fotos macht man mit take.
note.en: Photos take "take", not "make".

verbs.ex: I did some research on their company before the call.
The analysts conducted research with 200 companies.

note.de: Recherche macht man mit do oder conduct.
note.en: Research takes "do" or "conduct", not "make".

verbs.ex: We made good progress in the pilot this week.
The dashboard helps you track progress every day.

note.de: Fortschritte macht man mit make.
note.en: Progress takes "make", not "do".

verbs.ex: The team made a real effort to finish on time.
She put in a lot of effort to prepare the workshop.
We really appreciate your effort.

note.de: „Sich Mühe geben“ heißt make an effort.
note.en: You make an effort; "do" does not work here.

verbs.ex: We have done business with them for ten years.
Partners help us grow our business in the UK.
He runs a small business near Munich.

note.de: „Geschäfte machen“ heißt do business.
note.en: You do business with someone; you do not "make" business.

verbs.ex: We can make an exception for a pilot customer.
Finance granted an exception for this contract.

note.de: Ausnahmen macht man mit make.
note.en: Exceptions take "make", not "do".

verbs.ex: She gained a lot of experience in public sector sales.
Could you share your experience with the new archive?
We can draw on our experience from 300 projects.

note.de: „Erfahrungen machen“ heißt gain experience oder learn from experience.
note.en: You gain experience; "make experiences" is a literal translation.

verbs.ex: I had a good conversation with their CFO.
A good question is the easiest way to start a conversation.
It is hard to hold a conversation at a busy booth.

note.de: „Ein Gespräch führen“ heißt have a conversation.
note.en: You have a conversation; "lead" is a literal translation of "führen".

verbs.ex: The customer placed an order for 50 licenses.
They canceled the order after the budget cut.
We process orders within two days.

note.de: „Eine Bestellung aufgeben“ heißt place an order. Give an order ist ein Befehl.
note.en: You place an order; "give an order" means to command someone.

verbs.ex: We issue the invoice at the end of the month.
Please send the invoice to our accounts payable team.
Two managers have to approve every invoice.
They pay invoices within 30 days.

note.de: „Eine Rechnung stellen“ heißt issue oder send an invoice.
note.en: You issue or send an invoice; "put" is a literal translation of "stellen".

verbs.ex: We cannot take the risk of losing data.
Without backups, you run the risk of a long outage.
A pilot reduces the risk for both sides.

note.de: „Ein Risiko eingehen“ heißt take a risk.
note.en: You take a risk; "go" is a literal translation of "eingehen".

verbs.ex: The team met its sales target for the third quarter.
We hit our target two weeks early.
Let's set a realistic target for the pilot.

note.de: „Ein Ziel erfüllen“ heißt meet oder hit a target.
note.en: You meet or hit a target; "fulfill" does not go with target.

verbs.ex: The board approved the budget for next year.
They cut the IT budget by ten percent.
We managed to stay within the budget.

note.de: „Das Budget überziehen“ heißt go over budget oder exceed the budget.
note.en: You go over or exceed a budget; "overdraw" is for bank accounts.

verbs.ex: I made an appointment with the doctor for Monday.
Could we schedule an appointment for next week?
I had to cancel my appointment because of the trip.

note.de: „Einen Termin vereinbaren“ heißt make oder schedule an appointment.
note.en: You make or schedule an appointment; "agree an appointment" sounds foreign.

verbs.ex: It takes time to build a relationship with a new partner.
Regular calls help us maintain the relationship.
A joint event strengthened our relationship.

note.de: „Eine Beziehung pflegen“ heißt maintain oder nurture a relationship.
note.en: You maintain or nurture a relationship; "care" does not work here.

verbs.ex: I made contact with their IT manager at the trade show.
We established contact with three new resellers.
Let's stay in contact after the project.

note.de: „Kontakt aufnehmen“ heißt make contact oder get in touch.
note.en: You make contact or get in touch; "take up contact" is a literal translation.

verbs.ex: The security paper addresses the main concerns of IT.
The works council raised a concern about monitoring.
I share your concern about the timeline.

note.de: „Bedenken ausräumen“ heißt address oder resolve a concern.
note.en: You address or resolve a concern; "clear out" is a literal translation.

verbs.ex: Good sellers handle objections calmly.
A pilot helped us overcome the last objection.
The CFO raised an objection about the price.

note.de: „Einen Einwand entkräften“ heißt overcome oder address an objection.
note.en: You overcome or address an objection; "invalidate" sounds like a court ruling.

verbs.ex: After two hours, we reached a compromise.
Let's find a compromise that works for both sides.
They agreed on a compromise: 60 days.

note.de: „Einen Kompromiss schließen“ heißt reach a compromise.
note.en: You reach a compromise; "close" is a literal translation of "schließen".

verbs.ex: She manages our biggest accounts in southern Germany.
We won three new accounts this quarter.
We cannot afford to lose this account.

note.de: „Einen Kunden betreuen“ heißt manage an account.
note.en: You manage an account; "care for" is used for people and plants.

verbs.ex: We launched the project in January.
Who is going to manage the project on your side?
The project was completed on time and on budget.

note.de: „Ein Projekt durchführen“ heißt carry out oder run a project.
note.en: You carry out or run a project; "lead through" is a literal translation.

verbs.ex: We provide training for all new users.
Our consultant will run the training session on site.
All team leads attended the training.

note.de: „Eine Schulung machen“ heißt run a training session oder do some training. training ist unzählbar: nicht „a training“.
note.en: Say run a training session or do some training. Training is uncountable, so not "a training".

verbs.ex: Two partners showed interest in the program.
The webinar generated a lot of interest.
If the demo is too long, people lose interest.

note.de: „Interesse wecken“ heißt generate, spark oder arouse interest.
note.en: You generate or spark interest; "wake" is a literal translation of "wecken".

verbs.ex: The first call helps us identify the customer’s needs.
Our standard package meets the needs of most teams.
We assess your needs in a short workshop.

note.de: „Den Bedarf abfragen“ heißt identify oder assess the need. „Does this cover your needs?“ ist dagegen richtig.
note.en: To find out what a customer needs, you identify or assess the need. "Does this cover your needs?" is correct.

verbs.ex: The demo made a good impression on the board.
A short follow-up email leaves a professional impression.

note.de: „Einen Eindruck machen“ heißt make an impression. Do an impression heißt jemanden nachmachen.
note.en: You make an impression; "do an impression" means imitating someone.

verbs.ex: Could you give me an example from your industry?
Managers should set an example for their teams.

note.de: „Ein Beispiel nennen“ heißt give an example.
note.en: You give an example; "name" is a literal translation of "nennen".

verbs.ex: A pilot is a good first step to take.
Let's agree on the next steps before we hang up.
Please do not skip this step in the setup.

note.de: „Einen Schritt machen“ heißt take a step.
note.en: You take a step; "make" does not work here.

verbs.ex: Our support team handles complaints within 24 hours.
The customer filed a complaint about the delay.
We resolved the complaint with a phone call.

note.de: „Reklamation“ heißt complaint. Reclamation bedeutet Landgewinnung.
note.en: The German "Reklamation" is a complaint; "reclamation" means reclaiming land.

verbs.ex: We need to renew the license before March.
Can we extend the license to the HR team?
They purchased 200 licenses last year.

note.de: „Eine Lizenz verlängern“ heißt renew oder extend a license.
note.en: You renew or extend a license; "prolong" is rarely used for contracts.

verbs.ex: I will send you an email with the details.
Sorry for not answering your email sooner.
Could you forward the email to your IT manager?

note.de: „Auf eine Mail antworten“ heißt answer an email oder reply to an email.
note.en: You answer an email or reply to it; "answer on" is a literal translation.
